title: 🏛️ Exams 2001–2023 · modals in exam texts: meaning and form ⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2022, technical) A text about a young welder says: "She discovered her passion for working with her hands to fabricate works of art and things people could ___ ." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: After the modal "could" the verb stays in its base form: things people could use. A modal takes no -s and no -ing ending, so "uses" and "making" are wrong. "Ability" is a noun, not a verb, so it cannot follow a modal.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2022, technical) The same welder says: "My dad was a welder and I would ___ my free time in his workshop." Which form completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: "Would" works like the modals of this chapter: it is followed by the base verb alone, so I would spend. "Spent" and "spending" add an ending after a modal, and "to spend" adds a "to" that a modal never takes.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2023, technical) A text about a young electrician ends with this sentence: "You should never let society decide for you." Which function does the sentence express?
questions.explanation: "Should" + base verb gives advice: it is a good idea not to let others decide for you. The reader stays free to choose, so the sentence is not an obligation. It does not allow anything (permission) and it does not forbid anything (prohibition), even though "never" is in it.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2013, general) A nutritionist says about soft drinks: "Kids have to stop drinking soda." Which function does the statement express?
questions.explanation: "Have to" + base verb is one of the two ways of saying obligation, with must: stopping is necessary, the kids have no choice. A prohibition would use mustn't or Don't, a possibility would use may, might or could, and advice would use should.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2017, technical) A text about plumbing says: "You can't ___ new houses, offices, shopping centers or hospitals without plumbing." Which form completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: "Can't" is a modal, so it is followed by the base verb alone: you can't build. A modal never takes "to", "-ing" or "-s" after it. The sentence says that it is impossible to build without plumbing.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2015, technical) A teenager remembers how he discovered the Internet at school: "I was amazed by the different sites I ___ visit, especially music ones, emails and racing games." Which modal completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: He tells a story in the past and speaks of the sites that it was possible for him to visit: could + base verb. "Must" has no past form and would mean obligation, "can't" would deny that he visited them, which the rest of the sentence contradicts, and "could to" adds a "to".

questions.prompt: (Exam 2012, technical) A text about two friends who study at a technical school says: "John would like ___ join a large construction company." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: After "would like" the next verb needs "to": would like to join. "Like" is an ordinary verb, so unlike could or should it cannot be followed by the base verb alone. The other words leave "join" without its "to".

questions.prompt: (Exam 2005) A short text about giraffes says: "A large adult giraffe ___ be up to 6 meters ..." Pick the verb form that fits the gap.
questions.explanation: "Can" + base verb says what is possible for a giraffe: it can be up to 6 meters. A modal takes no -s and no "to" ("cans", "can to"). "Had to" would be a past obligation, which makes no sense for a fact about giraffes.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2017, general) A text on online shopping lists its disadvantages. It ends with: "Moreover, the description and the photos of the merchandise ___ be different from those of the real one." Which modal completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The sentence lists a disadvantage: it is possible that the photos do not match the real product. Possibility is said with may, might or could + base verb. "Should" would give advice, "have to" would say that the photos are obliged to be different, and "might to" wrongly adds "to".

questions.prompt: (Exam 2009, general) A text about our throw-away society says: "A lot of people don't think about the fact that something they are throwing away ___ be used by someone else. There may be some perfectly good and useful things in the landfills." Which modal completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The writer says that it is possible for a thrown-away object to be used again: could + base verb. "Cans" is wrong because a modal never takes -s. "Can't" says the opposite, and the next sentence speaks of perfectly good things. "Must" would mean obligation, not "perhaps".

questions.prompt: (Exam 2001) In a story, Emma lives in a village near London. "Emma was also a very clever girl. She believed she (could / can / will) change people's lives." Which modal completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: "Believed" is in the past, so the rest of the sentence stays in the past: she believed she could change people's lives. "Can" belongs to the present and "will" to the future, so neither fits a story told in the past. "Could to" adds a "to" that a modal never takes.
